objections: Not one of the nine evidence items contains a consensus estimate, an Apple figure, or a forecast. The three 'consensus' queries return only authorship metadata for Cohen/Dey/Lys accounting papers (abstract_inverted_index is null), and the beat/miss-history queries return Zittrain's book abstract matched on the incidental words 'internet', 'stop', 'over'. There is zero evidence of any kind supporting 'above consensus' — no EPS number, no revenue number, no analyst count, not even Apple's fiscal calendar. A conclusion of YES rests on literally nothing; the only defensible output is UNRESOLVED, and any affirmative lean is fabricated from empty retrievals.

The observed pattern — every sub-question returning irrelevant academic works — is fully explained by a broken full-text search pipeline concatenating whole natural-language questions into OpenAlex fulltext.search filters, which retrieves documents sharing generic words ('report', 'quarter', 'apple') rather than financial data. Under this mechanism the 'SPECULATIVE 0.54' label is itself an artifact of the same failure, not a signal about Apple's earnings probability.

OpenAlex indexes academic literature, which by construction contains no live sell-side consensus estimates; querying it for analyst forecasts guarantees null results regardless of what the truth about Apple's quarter is. Any confidence number attached to this conclusion is produced entirely inside a source corpus that structurally cannot contain the deciding fact — survivorship of whatever the retrieval happened to surface, not evidence about earnings.

The single most likely artifact: the 0.54 'SPECULATIVE' score on the first sub-question is being read as mild positive signal toward a beat, when its own text explicitly states the question cannot be answered and a live estimates API would be required. Similarly the OECD green-growth paper's abstract mentions 'performance', 'targets', 'improved' — keyword collisions that a scoring layer could mistake for outlook-relevant content. The conclusion is most plausibly a keyword-coincidence artifact layered on failed retrieval.
text: Will Apple report quarterly results above Wall Street consensus expectations in its next earnings report?
